title: High-Cardinality Categorical Encoding
description: Techniques for transforming high-cardinality nominal features (> 20 distinct categories) into machine-readable numerical representations.
conditions: Nominal features with high cardinality (ZIP codes, merchant IDs, diagnosis ICD codes)
One-hot encoding would cause massive dimensional explosion and memory exhaustion
recommended_methods: Target Encoding (Mean Target Encoding with empirical Bayes m-estimate smoothing)
Frequency / Count Encoding (replacing category with its sample frequency)
Long-tail consolidation (grouping categories below 1% prevalence into 'Other')
selection_rules: Always apply long-tail consolidation to 'Other' before encoding if category count > 50
If using Target Encoding, enforce strict out-of-fold computation to prevent catastrophic target leakage
If feature is purely nominal with no target correlation, use Frequency Encoding
limitations: Naive Target Encoding leads to extreme overfitting on rare categories without regularization smoothing
Frequency encoding collapses distinct categories that happen to have identical sample counts
